title: Abacavir enhances the efficacy of doxorubicin via inhibition of histone demethylase KDM5B in breast cancer.
authors: Jose, Anmi; Kulkarni, Pallavi; Kumar, Naveena An; Usman, Nawaz; Rodrigues, Gabriel Sunil; Shenoy, Gautham G; Damerla, Rama Rao; Munisamy, Murali; Bisht, Bharti; Varambally, Sooryanarayana; Paul, Manash K; Arya, Neha; Rao, Praveen Pn; Rao, Mahadev
one_liner_zh: 该文研究乳腺癌中KDM5B抑制与阿巴卡韦增敏多柔比星疗效，仅含分子对接提示药物代谢物与DNA聚合酶-DNA复合物互作，非TF-DNA结合体系且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联弱。
abstract: KDM5B, a lysine-specific histone demethylase, is widely upregulated in breast cancer. The current study investigated the role of KDM5B in breast cancer and explored the repurposing potential of the antiviral drug abacavir (ABC). The cytotoxic effects and the effect of ABC sensitization on doxorubicin (DOX) efficacy were evaluated using 2-D and 3-D cell culture models. KDM5B expression was elevated in breast cancer tissues compared to normal breast tissues. In vitro studies demonstrated that ABC treatment reduced KDM5B expression in breast cancer cells and increased their sensitivity towards DOX. ABC induced late apoptosis and S-phase arrest, while the ABC + DOX combination led to S/G2 phase arrest, late apoptosis, and cell death. Data generated from patient-derived breast tumoroids corroborated the 2-D cell culture-based findings. Additionally, molecular docking studies indicated that the active drug metabolite carbovir triphosphate (CBV-TP) could interact with the DNA polymerase beta-DNA complex, suggesting its potential mechanism to be incorporated into the DNA synthesis cycle, leading to cell cycle arrest in tumor cells. Our findings highlight the repurposing potential of ABC to target KDM5B in breast cancer. This approach enhanced the efficacy of DOX, which could allow further dose reduction and reduced side effects, offering a promising therapeutic strategy.
abstract_zh: KDM5B，一种赖氨酸特异性组蛋白去甲基化酶，在乳腺癌中广泛上调。本研究探讨了KDM5B在乳腺癌中的作用，并探索了抗病毒药物阿巴卡韦（ABC）的再利用潜力。通过二维和三维细胞培养模型评估了ABC的细胞毒性效应及其对阿霉素（DOX）疗效的增敏作用。与正常乳腺组织相比，乳腺癌组织中KDM5B表达升高。体外研究表明，ABC处理降低了乳腺癌细胞中KDM5B的表达，并增加了它们对DOX的敏感性。ABC诱导晚期凋亡和S期阻滞，而ABC + DOX联合治疗导致S/G2期阻滞、晚期凋亡和细胞死亡。来自患者来源的乳腺肿瘤类器官的数据证实了基于二维细胞培养的发现。此外，分子对接研究表明，活性药物代谢物卡波韦三磷酸（CBV-TP）能与DNA聚合酶β-DNA复合物相互作用，提示其可能通过掺入DNA合成周期导致肿瘤细胞周期阻滞的潜在机制。我们的发现强调了ABC在乳腺癌中靶向KDM5B的再利用潜力。这种方法增强了DOX的疗效，可能允许进一步减少剂量并降低副作用，提供了一种有前景的治疗策略。
